events.objective: Establish symptom onset and blast radius for the ~30% order submit failures: pin down when order-service error rate/504s started (precise time versus the v2.15.2 rollout), whether the 30% is uniform or concentrated on specific endpoints/instances/hosts, and which other services show simultaneous anomalies (latency, error rate, pool exhaustion, timeouts) between 09:00 and 13:00. Report the exact error signatures (e.g. downstream 504 vs local timeout vs connection refused) and which dependency the failing requests were waiting on.

Enumerate ALL changes in the window 2026-03-16T12:00Z to 2026-03-17T12:59Z across the whole estate, not just order-service: deployments (incl. order-service v2.15.2 and anything it depends on), config/feature-flag changes, and infrastructure changes. For each, give service, timestamp, and scope. Also map order-service's direct and transitive dependencies to identify shared components (gateway, DB, queue, auth, payment) that other services also use, and pull any historical incidents with matching symptoms (504s on order submit / 30% failure after a release) including what the actual root cause turned out to be.

Determine whether the fault is inside order-service v2.15.2 or downstream of it, and whether it is resource-driven: compare latency/error/resource metrics (CPU, memory, DB connections, thread/connection pool saturation, GC) for order-service and its downstream dependencies before vs after v2.15.2 went out; check whether the dependency's own metrics degrade at the same time or were already degrading beforehand, and whether the rollback (if visible) actually restored success rate. Use task a's onset time and task b's change list to anchor the comparison.

args.query: 504s order submit 30% failure rate after release

events.statement: The only deployment in the window 2026-03-16T12:00Z to 2026-03-17T12:59Z across ALL services is order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333), deployed 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z by a.khan, and it was already rolled back at 2026-03-17T11:16:00Z (status 'rolled_back'). Summary: 'Add idempotency keys to order submit'; changes: 'Idempotency-Key header persisted in orders table', 'retry-safe submit handler'.

The only config/feature-flag change in the window is pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds lowered 5 -> 4 (cfg-2290) at 2026-03-17T09:20:00Z by config-bot, i.e. ~1h28m BEFORE the order-service v2.15.2 deploy. pricing-engine is a direct HTTP dependency of order-service.

order-service dependency map (depth 3, downstream): directly depends on ledger-db (db), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http), kafka (queue-produce). Transitively: pricing-engine -> market-data-service (http) and -> redis-cache; market-data-service -> redis-cache and -> exchange-gateway; exchange-gateway -> exchange-api (external, has_telemetry=false).

Shared components in order-service's chain are used by other services too: ledger-db (postgres, shared=true) is used by portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service; redis-cache (shared=true) by auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service; kafka (shared=true) by payment-service, settlement-service and notification-service. api-gateway (edge) is the sole upstream caller of order-service (depth 2 found only api-gateway->order-service).

Historical precedent with matching symptoms: HIST-103 (2025-10-21) 'Order failures during exchange partner outage', services [order-service, exchange-gateway], symptoms ['504 on order submit','upstream timeouts']; its root cause was NOT a release: 'External exchange API outage on the partner side' (category dependency_failure), resolved by failing over to a secondary exchange route. Other 'failure after release' precedents: HIST-101 auth-service (bcrypt cost 10->14), HIST-109 auth-service (JWT library clock-skew default) — both bad_deployment resolved by rollback.

order-service produced the only deployment and no infra change appears in the window; the only infrastructure-change precedent in history is HIST-107 (2025-12-09, redis primary failover -> cache miss storm, shared redis-cache also used by pricing-engine/market-data-service) and HIST-104 (Kafka broker rebalance). The two events nearest the reported onset (11:10Z) before it are the 09:20Z pricing cache-TTL change (~1h28m prior) and the 10:48Z order-service deploy (~22m prior).

events.description: Could not run infra-change / rollback event queries beyond what get_deployments and get_config_changes returned; deployments returned count=1 and config returned count=1 with no warnings, but no dedicated infra (node/cluster/db failover/restart) change feed was queried, so a non-deployment infrastructure change (e.g. redis failover, kafka rebalance like HIST-104/107) in the window cannot be ruled out.

Did not query the health metrics / logs of shared components (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka, exchange-gateway, exchange-api) in the window, since this task was scoped to change enumeration and dependency mapping.

Historical search returned only 6 incidents; no HIST entry matched '30% failure rate after release' on order-service exactly (closest symptom match HIST-103 was an external dependency failure, and the bad-deployment precedents were auth-service).

events.answer: In the 2026-03-16T12:00Z–2026-03-17T12:59Z window the whole estate shows exactly ONE deployment (order-service v2.15.2, dep-5333, deployed 10:48Z, rolled back 11:16Z) and ONE config change (pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5→4 at 09:20Z, cfg-2290). No other service in the estate deployed or changed config. order-service's dependency chain is api-gateway → order-service → {ledger-db (shared Postgres), pricing-engine → {market-data-service, redis-cache (shared)}, exchange-gateway → exchange-api (external vendor)}, plus kafka (shared queue). Shared components used by other services: ledger-db (portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service), redis-cache (auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service), kafka (payment-service, settlement-service, notification-service). Historical match: HIST-103 (2025-10-21) had identical symptoms of 504s on order submit, and its actual root cause was an EXTERNAL exchange API outage — not the release.

events.statement: order-service error rate is flat ~0.17–0.25% from 08:00 through 10:48, then steps to 8.02% at 10:56 and settles at ~30–31.5% (30.44 at 11:04) and stays there through 12:56 — a sharp step change, not a ramp.
All 349 order-service ERROR logs in 11:02:45–12:58:54 carry a single pattern: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'; the earliest is orderId=07fcb25a at 11:02:45.

exchange-gateway shows the anomaly earlier than order-service: its first ERROR is at 11:01:25 and error_rate jumps from ~0.21% baseline to 39.89% in the 11:00 bucket (peak 48.42%); p99 latency jumps from ~130ms to 5085ms avg at 11:04.

exchange-gateway's own upstream call is the failing dependency: logs show 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' (163) and op=quoteSnapshot (146), plus 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' (161); upstream_latency_ms jumps from ~118ms to ~8408ms avg at 11:00 (max 10042ms).
The 30% failure is ~uniform across time, not spiky: order-service error_rate buckets stay tightly in 30.44–31.64% for every bucket from 11:04 to 12:56 (max never above ~35.6%).

order-service's own error log onset (11:02:45) lags exchange-gateway's (11:01:25) by ~80s, consistent with the failure originating downstream at the exchange-gateway/partner boundary rather than inside order-service; this ordering is a data observation, the causal direction is inference.

events.description: Could not compare onset against the v2.15.2 rollout time: no deploy/release-event telemetry was available in these tools, so whether the release preceded the 11:01 first error cannot be confirmed from data.

Running out of call budget before checking other services (api-gateway, payment-service, settlement-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka, exchange-api) for simultaneous 09:00–13:00 anomalies.
No per-instance/per-host or per-endpoint breakdown was retrieved (only aggregate service-level metrics); the failure looks time-uniform but instance/host concentration was not measured.

events.answer: Order submit failures are a clean step change: order-service error rate jumps from ~0.2% baseline to ~30% starting in the 10:56–11:04 window (~11:00), with the first-observed error log at 11:02:45. The uniform signature for all 349 order-service errors is `exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)` — i.e. the failure is a downstream/exchange-gateway timeout, not a local order-service fault, and it is ~uniform (~30–31% every bucket) rather than spiky. exchange-gateway degrades first (first error 11:01:25, error rate 0.21%→~44%, p99 130ms→~5100ms) and its upstream `api.exchange-partner.example` connect timeouts (5000ms) plus 503s are the earliest signal; the v2.15.2 rollout correlation could not be confirmed from telemetry (no deploy event data available to me).

events.statement: order-service shows NO local resource saturation at or after onset: cpu_pct is flat ~39-40% avg (max 45.44%) across all buckets 09:00-12:56 (e.g. 39.91 avg at 10:50, 39.78 at 11:00, 40.08 at 11:10), and memory_pct is flat ~58-62% avg (max 67.93%) with no step at 11:00. db_pool_in_use is flat ~14 connections (13.85 avg at 11:00, 14.04 at 11:10; max 15.49 over the whole window) — no pool exhaustion.

order-service latency p99 steps abruptly at the 11:00 bucket from a flat ~147-153ms baseline (150.67 avg at 10:40, 149.93 at 10:50) to 4285.85ms avg (max 5631.42) and stays ~5200-5400ms through 12:50. The ~5.2s plateau matches the 5000ms upstream connect timeout, i.e. requests are blocking on a downstream dependency, not on local CPU/memory/DB.

exchange-gateway, the failing dependency, also shows no resource driving the fault: cpu_pct flat ~29-30% avg (max 33.58%) and memory_pct flat ~44% avg (max 48.99%) across 09:00-12:56, unchanged through onset. So the gateway's degradation is not CPU/memory-driven.

exchange-gateway's failures continue unchanged long after the order-service rollback (11:16Z): logs from 11:20:03Z to 12:58:32Z still show 396 ERROR entries with the same three patterns — 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' (140), 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' (133), and '... op=quoteSnapshot' (123). The downstream failure signature persists ~1h42m past the rollback.

The fault is NOT inside order-service v2.15.2 and is not resource-driven: order-service's own resources (CPU, memory, DB pool) are all flat across the deploy and onset, while its only error signature is the downstream 504 (per T1/F8) and its p99 plateau equals the downstream 5000ms timeout. The downstream exchange-gateway to external api.exchange-partner.example (has_telemetry=false) boundary is where 503s/timeouts originate, and it keeps failing after the rollback. This mirrors HIST-103 (external exchange API outage, not a release).

Could not directly verify whether the 11:16Z rollback restored order-service success rate: the error_rate query restricted to 11:00-12:59 for order-service was not executed (tool-call budget exhausted). Contextual evidence from T1/F7/F11 and tc-020 is that error rate stayed ~30-31% through 12:56 and exchange-gateway kept erroring through 12:58, i.e. the rollback did not clear the symptom.

events.description: order-service error_rate for the 11:00-12:59 window (to confirm whether the 11:16Z rollback changed anything at fine granularity) was not executed — tool-call budget exhausted.

ledger-db error_rate query returned not_found; the DB exposes only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min, so its health could not be assessed with the intended metric.
api.exchange-partner.example has has_telemetry=false, so the external partner's own latency/error metrics could not be measured directly — only its symptoms via exchange-gateway logs.

No deployment-marker metric (restarts) was queried for order-service, so I cannot quantify whether the v2.15.2 rollback triggered pod restarts or whether the release even took effect on the serving instances.

events.answer: The fault is downstream of order-service v2.15.2 and is not resource-driven. order-service's own CPU (~40%), memory (~60%) and DB pool (~14 conns) are flat across the deploy and the ~11:00 onset, while its p99 jumps from ~150ms to a ~5.2s plateau matching the downstream 5000ms timeout — its only error is the 504 from exchange-gateway (per T1/F8). exchange-gateway (flat CPU ~30%, memory ~44%) is failing at its external upstream api.exchange-partner.example (503s + 5000ms connect timeouts), and those errors persist from 11:01 through 12:58 — well past the order-service rollback at 11:16Z — so the rollback did not restore success rate.

pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds config change (cfg-2290) degraded a shared path feeding order-service
Shared infrastructure component (redis-cache failover or kafka rebalance) degraded at onset, indirectly breaking the order path

tasks.objective: Establish symptom onset and blast radius for the ~30% order submit failures: pin down when order-service error rate/504s started (precise time versus the v2.15.2 rollout), whether the 30% is uniform or concentrated on specific endpoints/instances/hosts, and which other services show simultaneous anomalies (latency, error rate, pool exhaustion, timeouts) between 09:00 and 13:00. Report the exact error signatures (e.g. downstream 504 vs local timeout vs connection refused) and which dependency the failing requests were waiting on.
tasks.answer: Order submit failures are a clean step change: order-service error rate jumps from ~0.2% baseline to ~30% starting in the 10:56–11:04 window (~11:00), with the first-observed error log at 11:02:45. The uniform signature for all 349 order-service errors is `exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)` — i.e. the failure is a downstream/exchange-gateway timeout, not a local order-service fault, and it is ~uniform (~30–31% every bucket) rather than spiky. exchange-gateway degrades first (first error 11:01:25, error rate 0.21%→~44%, p99 130ms→~5100ms) and its upstream `api.exchange-partner.example` connect timeouts (5000ms) plus 503s are the earliest signal; the v2.15.2 rollout correlation could not be confirmed from telemetry (no deploy event data available to me).

Also map order-service's direct and transitive dependencies to identify shared components (gateway, DB, queue, auth, payment) that other services also use, and pull any historical incidents with matching symptoms (504s on order submit / 30% failure after a release) including what the actual root cause turned out to be.
tasks.answer: In the 2026-03-16T12:00Z–2026-03-17T12:59Z window the whole estate shows exactly ONE deployment (order-service v2.15.2, dep-5333, deployed 10:48Z, rolled back 11:16Z) and ONE config change (pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5→4 at 09:20Z, cfg-2290). No other service in the estate deployed or changed config. order-service's dependency chain is api-gateway → order-service → {ledger-db (shared Postgres), pricing-engine → {market-data-service, redis-cache (shared)}, exchange-gateway → exchange-api (external vendor)}, plus kafka (shared queue). Shared components used by other services: ledger-db (portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service), redis-cache (auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service), kafka (payment-service, settlement-service, notification-service). Historical match: HIST-103 (2025-10-21) had identical symptoms of 504s on order submit, and its actual root cause was an EXTERNAL exchange API outage — not the release.

tasks.objective: Determine whether the fault is inside order-service v2.15.2 or downstream of it, and whether it is resource-driven: compare latency/error/resource metrics (CPU, memory, DB connections, thread/connection pool saturation, GC) for order-service and its downstream dependencies before vs after v2.15.2 went out; check whether the dependency's own metrics degrade at the same time or were already degrading beforehand, and whether the rollback (if visible) actually restored success rate. Use task a's onset time and task b's change list to anchor the comparison.
tasks.answer: The fault is downstream of order-service v2.15.2 and is not resource-driven. order-service's own CPU (~40%), memory (~60%) and DB pool (~14 conns) are flat across the deploy and the ~11:00 onset, while its p99 jumps from ~150ms to a ~5.2s plateau matching the downstream 5000ms timeout — its only error is the 504 from exchange-gateway (per T1/F8). exchange-gateway (flat CPU ~30%, memory ~44%) is failing at its external upstream api.exchange-partner.example (503s + 5000ms connect timeouts), and those errors persist from 11:01 through 12:58 — well past the order-service rollback at 11:16Z — so the rollback did not restore success rate.
